描述_ZN: Wutong Cat and Butterfly Painting Axis, Modern, painted by Xu Beihong, on paper with color, 91.5 cm in length and 60.9 cm in width.　　Self-titled: "In June in Yuzhou, I thanked my brother Zhiliu for making up a vivid butterfly for me, the view in front of the window of the Chinese Literature and Art Society. I was bored in the heat and wrote this to amuse myself. Beihong." The lower right corner of the painting is inscribed with a square seal in vermilion, "Washing and playing".　　This picture is a joint work of Xu Beihong and Xie Zhiliu for pleasure. Xie Zhiliu (1910-1997), character Zhuangmu, was an expert in calligraphy and painting, as well as in painting and calligraphy theory and appraisal. During the War of Resistance against Japan, Xie Zhiliu lived in Chongqing, where he was a professor in the art department of the Central University and a member of the China Literature and Art Society with Xu Beihong. The China Literature and Art Society was founded in Guanyin Rock, Chongqing during the war, and was chaired by Mr. Hua Lin. In 1945, Xie Zhiliu was introduced to Xu Beihong by the famous painter Zhang Daqian. Xu was quite impressed with Xie Zhiliu's erudition and talent.　　A long-haired cat finds a butterfly resting through a gap in the leaves, and is eager to catch it. The picture is vivid and interesting.　　The carving of the wutong leaves in the picture is very characteristic, first with intermittent ink lines outlining the edges, and then with a mixture of full-blown blue and yellow, green haloing the leaf surface, and while wet painting the stems and veins of the leaves. The outline and rendering are integrated, and the water and color and ink are blended to bring out the light and moist texture of the leaves.
